title.en: Product support site (help centre, changelog, status)
title.tr: Urun destek sitesi (yardim merkezi, yenilikler, durum)

summary: The companion sites of a software product: a help centre with instant search, categories and articles; a changelog with release filters and subscribe; and a public status page with components, uptime bars, incidents and history. Each part is independent: build only the parts the business runs (often each on its own subdomain), and treat the first page of each part as its home.

pages.purpose: Help-centre home: one big search that answers while the visitor types, the topics, the most-read articles and how to reach a person.

sections.purpose: Large search field whose results appear under it as you type: articles with the match highlighted, matching categories and an 'ask support with these words' row.
fields: Article index: titles, keywords, summaries, category
Where 'ask support' sends the typed question
sections.notes: No results page and no Enter needed; arrows move, Enter opens, Escape closes, '/' focuses. Rank by whole query at the start of a title word, then title words, keywords, summary; highlight only matches at word starts and fold diacritics. Results count announced via aria-live. A quiet line with the current service status (linked to the status page) can sit under the field.

sections.purpose: Six or so topic cards, each with icon, one line and article count.
alternatives: card: when each topic needs a few top articles listed inside the card
fields: Per category: name, icon, one-line description, number of articles

sections.purpose: Most-read articles, so common questions are one click away.
alternatives: blog-list: articles with excerpts and update dates
fields: Most-read article titles, category, last updated date

sections.purpose: How to reach support when the articles do not answer: channels, hours and expected reply time.
fields: Support channels (chat, email, form, phone, community)

pages.purpose: One topic: its articles with a filter, the other topics beside it.

sections.purpose: Category title, description and breadcrumb back to the help home.
Articles of the category with a filter field; the other categories as a side list.
sections.notes: Filter folds diacritics; show an empty state that offers to ask support. Shareable link per category.

pages.purpose: One answer: steps as an ordered list, then 'was this helpful', related articles and contact.

sections.purpose: The article with a compact search above it.
fields: Body with headings in order, steps as an ordered list, screenshots with alt text
sections.notes: Keep headings in order so readers jump by heading; show the updated date.

sections.purpose: 'Was this helpful?': yes thanks, no asks what was missing (reasons plus an optional note).
Next articles to read and the way to support.

pages.purpose: Changelog home: every release in a narrow editorial column with its date pinned beside it, filterable by kind, with email and RSS subscribe.

sections.purpose: What this changelog covers, release cadence and subscribe.
fields: Product name and what is covered

sections.purpose: Release list with feature / improvement / fix filters; each release's date and version stay pinned beside it while it scrolls.
alternatives: activity-timeline: a short log without per-release pages
fields: Per release: version, ISO date, title, changes tagged by kind, link to the release page
sections.notes: Wide screens: sticky date rail beside each release; narrow screens: a date bar under the navbar follows the release in view. Hide releases with nothing left after filtering and announce the filter result in a status region. Use real dates in each heading.

sections.purpose: Email subscription (validated, with a confirmation state) and the RSS feed with a copy button.
fields: What subscribers get and how often
sections.notes: RSS alone can stay without the newsletter feature.

pages.purpose: One release as an article: a section per kind of change, a code sample when relevant, the upgrade note, older / newer links.

sections.purpose: The release body.
fields: Upgrade / migration note for breaking changes

sections.purpose: Older and newer release links, then subscribe.

pages.purpose: Status home: is it working right now, what is broken, what is planned and how reliable each part has been.

sections.purpose: Overall banner (status-coloured edge, one summary line), then the active incident with its latest updates and any scheduled maintenance.
fields: Active incidents: title, impact, affected components, updates with times
Scheduled maintenance: window, components, what to expect
sections.notes: Banner is a role=status live region. Status pills keep the colour in the dot and the text at full contrast (status colours are not reliable as small text).

sections.purpose: Components in groups, each with its state and 90 daily uptime bars plus the uptime percentage.
fields: Daily uptime per component for 90 days
sections.notes: One tab stop per row; arrows, Home and End move between days with a tooltip (date, uptime, incidents) tied by aria-describedby; Enter on a day with an incident opens it. Include a legend of states.

sections.purpose: Latency of the main API over the last days, plus recently resolved incidents.
fields: Daily p95 latency for the main endpoint
sections.notes: Give the chart a text summary.

sections.purpose: Get notified by email, webhook or RSS, only for incidents and maintenance.
fields: How often messages are sent on average

pages.purpose: One incident: what was hit and for how long, every update, and the postmortem when there is one.

sections.purpose: Impact, affected components, start, end and duration.
fields: Incident title, impact, components, start / end times with time zone

sections.purpose: Every update newest first (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved).
fields: Updates with stage, time and text

sections.purpose: Cause, impact, what was done and what changes.

pages.purpose: Every incident and maintenance of the last 90 days, by month, filterable by component group.

sections.purpose: Period covered.
Incidents and maintenance grouped by month with a component-group filter.
fields: Past incidents with impact, components, duration and link
sections.notes: Months without incidents say so instead of disappearing.

content: Which parts the business runs: help centre, changelog, status page (and their domains)
Help articles with titles, keywords, summaries, categories and update dates
Help categories with icons and descriptions
Support channels, hours, time zone and reply times
Where article feedback and support questions go
Release history: versions, dates, change kinds, upgrade notes
RSS feed and email subscription setup
Uptime data source (monitoring tool) and incident history
Incident and maintenance update process and postmortem policy

styles.name: calm civic help
styles.why: Help centres: an open, readable sans, quick and out-of-the-way motion, results dropping under the field.

styles.name: narrow editorial notes
styles.why: Changelogs read as a column of dated articles; a serif and a deep accent make each release feel published.

styles.name: neutral compact status
styles.why: Status pages: information first, a neutral accent so only status colours carry meaning; the live dot is the only loop.

pitfalls: A status page hosted on the same infrastructure as the product goes down with it; host it separately.
Status colour as the only signal, or coloured small text that fails contrast; pair every state with a word and an icon.
Uptime bars that cannot be read by keyboard or screen reader; give each day a tooltip and a text alternative.
Incident times without a time zone, or incidents quietly removed from history.
Help search that needs Enter and a results page, or misses words with diacritics.
Articles without an updated date or with steps as prose instead of an ordered list.
Changelog entries without real dates, or breaking changes without an upgrade note.
Subscribe forms without a confirmation state and clear consent for what will be sent.
